caption:
Gartner forecast that by 2026, 20% of organisations would use AI to cut half their middle-management roles. Fifteen weeks left in that year.

When layers come out of an org chart, the decision is not made on spreadsheets alone. Someone in a closed room points at a name and says: I can see them in the bigger job. That sentence is built long before the meeting. It is built in how you enter a room, how you hold a pause, whether your voice carries the weight of your own decision.

Competence keeps you employed. Command presence keeps you visible. In a flattening, visible is the only category that survives.

Thirty-five years of military command taught Colonel Suhag one thing about authority: it is a set of behaviours, not a personality. Bearing. Tone. Calculated silence. Trainable, all three.

Do the work now, while there is still a layer to stand on.

topic.title: The Great Flattening: 2026 is middle management's deadline year
topic.angle: This audience *is* middle and senior management, and when layers are removed the survivors are the ones leadership can see and picture in a bigger room — making executive presence structural job security rather than a nice-to-have.
topic.why_now: Gartner's widely-cited forecast that 20% of organisations would use AI to cut 50% of middle-management roles set 2026 as the deadline, and there are roughly 15 weeks left in that year to say "the year they said half of us would be gone."

rationale: A stark, text-only visual matches the caption's blunt deadline framing without diluting the seriousness of a layoff-cycle topic.
